approach.method_basis: The Parent is a genetic algorithm over molecular graphs that uses a Gaussian-process model to decide which offspring get scored. It keeps the 64 best scored molecules, draws breeders mostly from the top score quantiles, and builds about 160 fresh candidates per round by connected-fragment crossover and atom, bond and ring mutations. A Gaussian process fitted only to this session's own scores, using counted Morgan substructure environments and a Tanimoto-style kernel, predicts every candidate. Ten correlated Thompson samples from its joint posterior then pick the ten molecules to evaluate, one per sample, never picking the same molecule twice. The width of those samples is the model's posterior uncertainty in units of the observed score spread, and it is the same in every round. Admission rules keep stable molecular identities, reject duplicates, and block new unusual sulfur environments that the scored parents did not already contain.
approach.novelty: This Child makes the width of the Thompson samples depend on whether the search is stuck. When the best score has not improved for three consecutive rounds of ten evaluations, it widens the samples by a fixed factor of 1.5 around the same predictions, so candidates the model is less sure about win more of the ten slots. The first round that improves the best score restores the Parent's sampler exactly, and every run is identical to the Parent's until its first stall. Earlier children of this Parent removed the sampled spread entirely or removed its correlation across candidates, and both lost; an earlier experiment in this lineage rescaled the spread for the whole run from its prediction errors and also lost. None tied exploration to a measured stall. The concurrent siblings use the same stall signal to change mutation length, candidate breadth or crossover instead of the sampler.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-1744a1494180 (complete panel mean 0.596453, population SD 0.033970; per-task means zaleplon_mpo 0.4568, deco_hop 0.7069, drd2_docking 0.9910, median_2 0.2227, sitagliptin_mpo 0.6048) spends a measurable share of its budget stalled while its allocator keeps exactly the same exploration width. Re-deriving the shared trigger from its own published trajectories (runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-1744a1494180/seed-0|1|2/trajectories/<task>.jsonl, 300 records each) reproduces the ticket exactly: with K=3 consecutive non-improving announced batches the regime is entered in 13 of 15 sessions (29 episodes, 91 of 435 batches; never in deco_hop seeds 0 and 2); K=2 gives 15/15 sessions, 51 episodes, 140 batches and K=4 gives 12/15, 21, 62. Mean per-session best-so-far gain decays +0.2402 / +0.1054 / +0.0424 over evaluations 11-100 / 101-200 / 201-300 (5.819415 total). Inside the K=3 regime only 25 of 91 batches raise the incumbent (27%, against 196 of 435 = 45% overall); episodes resolve after a mean of 3.2 regime batches including the resolving batch (25 resolved, 4 terminal-censored; drd2_docking seed 1 sits at the 1.0 ceiling), and summed incumbent gain inside the regime is 0.4766. The sampled residual is a measured positive component of this Parent: removing it costs -0.116317 (n-f04cec6ab705) and removing only its cross-candidate correlation costs -0.050545 (n-8df0bb3bbcfe), mirroring -0.076861 (n-299096e31fe7) and -0.018447 (n-54adc6a641e8) on n-62daf219c70a, while a whole-run prequential rescaling with multipliers 0.586-2.849 lost -0.038141 (n-38bcd7569cce). Whether its amplitude should depend on the search state is untested. A read-only replay of the Parent's logged posterior_pool, posterior_selection and offspring_observed events (runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-1744a1494180/seed-*/logs/<task>.log; zero mismatches against its actual choices at factor 1.0) sizes the lever and the risk. In the 91 stalled batches a factor of 1.5 on the same normals changes all 91 selected sets and 294 of 910 selected identities, moving the median within-pool posterior-mean percentile of picks from 0.912 to 0.780 and the median posterior-SD percentile from 0.296 to 0.453 (factor 2.0 would change 456 identities and move them to 0.610 and 0.616). On the realized stalled stream, picks in the top 3% of posterior mean produced 21 of 34 incumbent-beating offspring (9.0% versus 1.9% for all other picks) and 0.343 of 0.567 positive incumbent margin, and the 43 picks in the top posterior-SD decile produced none. The Parent's nominal 95% predictive intervals cover 78.7% of stalled-regime outcomes (75.1% elsewhere), a Gaussian-equivalent under-dispersion of about 1.24 (median-based) to 1.58 (coverage-based). These stream associations are selection-conditioned and unselected alternatives carry no labels, so they bound the dose and state the prior risk; they do not decide whether wider sampling during stalls converts stalled batches into gain.

deviations.adopted_setting: One factor fixed before evaluation from the Parent's stalled-regime calibration and passive replay.
deviations.paper_setting: Alpha values compared as tuning settings over many simulated runs.
deviations.reason: The protocol allows one exposed complete panel for this recipe and forbids a factor sweep.

adoptions.implementation_change: Inside FingerprintPosterior.select, stall-allocated batches use samples = mean + (score_scale * 1.5) * (normals @ factor.T): means, Cholesky factor and normals are unchanged and the sample variance is multiplied by 2.25.

literature_review.conclusion: The sources supply the trigger construction (a consecutive-failure counter reset on success), the schedule shape (raise exploration only after a run of unsuccessful steps and restore it at the first strict improvement) and the operation (widen Thompson samples around an unchanged mean). They do not establish that widening Thompson sampling during stagnation helps: TuRBO answers consecutive failures by contracting its trust region, and Chapelle and Li found sharper rather than wider posteriors often lowered non-asymptotic regret. The factor 1.5 therefore rests on internal evidence from the Parent's receipts (stalled-regime under-dispersion of 1.24 to 1.58; a replay showing it changes about a third of stalled choices while displacing fewer top-mean picks than 2.0), and the experiment is a genuine two-sided test of one dose.

stagnation detection evolutionary algorithm increase mutation strength after unsuccessful steps Rajabi Witt
Thompson sampling posterior variance scaling inflation exploration empirical evaluation Chapelle Li 2011

sources.applicability: Supplies the batch-level consecutive-failure bookkeeping reset by success that the shared stall trigger uses. Its response to failure is contraction toward exploitation, the opposite of widening, so it is a competing design and a reason the sign is open, not support for this direction.
sources.finding: TuRBO defines a success as a candidate that improves on the incumbent and a failure as one that does not, counts consecutive successes and failures, doubles the trust-region side after tau_succ consecutive successes, halves it after tau_fail consecutive failures, resets the counters after each size change and restarts a region whose side falls below L_min; batches inside each region are chosen by Thompson sampling.
sources.title: Scalable Global Optimization via Local Bayesian Optimization (Eriksson, Pearce, Gardner, Turner, Poloczek; NeurIPS 2019)

sources.applicability: Supplies the schedule shape adopted here: default behaviour until a threshold of unsuccessful steps, raised exploration strength while stuck, restoration at the first strict improvement. Its runtime theory concerns pseudo-Boolean Hamming gaps and does not transfer to a molecular Thompson allocator.
sources.finding: Stagnation detection (SD-(1+1) EA) counts iterations without improvement, raises the mutation strength from r to r+1 once the count exceeds a strength-dependent threshold, and resets both counter and strength (to 0 and 1) as soon as a strict improvement is found, so increased exploration is spent only while the search is stuck.
sources.title: Self-Adjusting Evolutionary Algorithms for Multimodal Optimization (Rajabi and Witt; GECCO 2020, arXiv 2004.03266)

sources.applicability: Supplies the operation: widen the sampling spread around an unchanged posterior mean. Its whole-run results argue against unconditional widening, consistent with the ended prequential loss, which is why only a stall-conditioned widening remains an open test here.
sources.finding: Posterior reshaping draws Thompson samples from a sharpened or widened posterior with the mean unchanged (Beta parameters divided by alpha); alpha below 1 often gave lower non-asymptotic regret at the price of occasional very large regret, and an optimistic variant gave only a marginal gain because with many arms the selected arm already carries a boosted sample.
sources.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Thompson Sampling (Chapelle and Li; NIPS 2011)

hypothesis: State-conditioned Thompson residual amplitude: while the session's consecutive non-improving announced-batch counter is at least 3, multiply only the sampled residual of the correlated Thompson fresh-pool allocation, score_scale * (standard_normals @ Cholesky_factor.T), by the fixed constant 1.5 (sample variance x2.25 around the unchanged count-GP posterior means), so the ten sequentially masked argmax choices of a stalled batch move from high-mean, low-uncertainty pool members toward higher-uncertainty members. The factor is exactly 1.0 before the first stall and again from the batch after the first strictly improving batch; the posterior mean, kernel, normalization, noise, covariance, Cholesky factor, normal draws, masks and ties are unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Wider stall-time sampling changed a third of stalled picks, but the swapped-in molecules scored worse and the panel lost 0.0097
finding_summary.insights:
Widening the Thompson draws while the search is stuck does what it says. It reliably moves picks toward molecules the model is unsure about. But on this Anchor those molecules are worse bets, not hidden opportunities. At this dose, the exact same-pool comparison at the first stall contradicts the hope behind this experiment: the uncertain tail did not hold untapped value that a stall-time boost could convert into gain. In the Parent, incumbent improvements during stalls came mostly from high-mean, low-uncertainty picks (21 of 34 incumbent beats came from the top 3% of predicted score and none from the most uncertain tenth), and those are the picks the wider sampling gave up. The inherited amplitude is therefore at least as good as 1.5 even under measured stagnation, and a larger factor or a lower threshold would swap in more of the same kind of pick. The registered recipe ends here, and no factor or threshold sweep is justified.

The chemistry offers a concrete reason. The molecular review found Child and Parent output nearly indistinguishable except for more 1-4 heavy-atom fragments (139 against 97 of 4,350). That entire excess sits in stalled batches: 69 of 1,070 stalled evaluations against 22 of 910 for the Parent, and 44 of the 356 swapped-in picks. Fragments score at the floor and are what the model is least sure about, so uncertainty-boosting allocation spends budget on them unless emission screens them out. The result also narrows the stagnation question to its other side. TuRBO-style contraction, meaning sharper sampling during stalls, is untested here, and this node does not show that it would help, although the evidence that top-mean picks carry stalled-regime gains is consistent with it. Still open: why zaleplon_mpo absorbs most of the loss, and whether the higher in-stall gain on sitagliptin and median_2 was added gain or merely gain moved from unstalled batches into stalled ones. The siblings using the same trigger with other channels remain dependent comparisons on the same Parent and seeds.
finding_summary.results:
The change ran exactly as registered. Every session was identical to the Parent until its first stalled batch: same candidate pools, same random draws, same picks. The two deco_hop sessions that never stalled reproduced the Parent's runs record for record. Inside stalled batches the sampled noise was exactly 1.5 times the Parent's, and outside them it was exactly unchanged. The Child spent 107 of 435 batches in the stalled regime over 36 episodes in 13 of 15 sessions, against 91 batches and 29 episodes for the Parent. In those batches the widened sampling changed the chosen set in 105 of 107 batches and swapped 356 of 1,070 picks, about the one third the pre-run replay predicted. Choices moved as intended. The median pick fell from the 92nd to the 78th percentile of predicted score, and rose from the 32nd to the 49th percentile of model uncertainty. Outside stalls no pick changed.

The extra exploration did not produce more gain. The cleanest test is the first stalled batch of each session, where Child and Parent faced the identical pool and the Parent actually scored the molecules the Child dropped. There the best new score was identical in all 13 sessions. The 43 molecules the wider sampling swapped in averaged 0.182, while the 43 they displaced averaged 0.363, and the swapped-in set was worse in 12 of 13 sessions. Across all stalled batches, a stalled batch raised the session best 27.1% of the time, against 27.5% for the Parent. Swapped-in picks beat their best parent 3.4% of the time, against 10.6% for the picks both rules agreed on. Summed gain inside stalls did rise, from 0.477 to 0.603, and resolved stalls ended slightly sooner (2.93 batches against 3.20). But that sum grew because the Child was stalled longer: gain per stalled batch was essentially flat, and more stalls ran out of budget unresolved (7 against 4). From the first trigger onward, over the same 2,340 evaluations, the Child realized less best-score gain than the Parent (0.894 against 1.039) and fewer parent-beating offspring (230 against 261).

The complete matched panel mean fell from 0.5965 to 0.5867, a paired change of -0.0097 against the required +0.002, and all three seed macros were lower. Five cells rose, seven fell and three tied: the two never-stalled deco_hop sessions, plus one sitagliptin session that ended level. Most of the loss sits in zaleplon_mpo, the task that stalls most: it fell in all three seeds (-0.065, -0.034, -0.034) after 41 stalled batches against the Parent's 33, and its gain inside stalls fell from 0.152 to 0.052. The other ten exposed cells average about -0.001; that is a sensitivity note, not a substitute for the panel.

molecular.headline: Mid-size fused heteroaromatics decorated with single halogens; leaders carry N-F or O-F bonds, four-membered rings and aminals
molecular.overall_character: Across the five objectives the node proposed 870 optimizer molecules per task (4,350 in total; Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 evaluations each, 10 of them the shared initial molecules) and every proposal parses as a valid neutral molecule. They are medium-sized and heavily cyclic: mean 23.6-32.6 heavy atoms, MW 354-470, 2.92-4.76 rings of which 2.06-3.79 are aromatic, consistent with the digest counters (ring_closure_rate 0.947-0.982, aromatic_atom_rate 0.938-0.969, branch_rate 0.945-0.978). Elaboration is almost entirely peripheral: a fused heteroaromatic or bridged polycyclic core is decorated with methyl, ethyl, propyl, methoxy, hydroxymethyl, acetyl, nitroso, aldehyde and above all single halogen atoms (digest halogen_rate 0.75-0.98 on four tasks, 0.108 on the fifth). Halogen goes onto heteroatoms as readily as onto carbon: 818 of the 4,350 proposals contain an N-halogen bond and 378 an O-halogen bond, while not one of the 4,350 contains a trifluoromethyl group and the largest fluorine count reached anywhere is six atoms in a single molecule. No proposal carries a formal charge and none carries written stereochemistry (digest charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five tasks), yet RDKit finds unassigned stereocentres in 30.3, 49.0, 95.1, 75.6 and 68.0 percent of the five sets and in 87 of 87 top-decile molecules on one of them. Ring chemistry is abundant but not always feasible: four-membered rings appear in 9.5-37.1 percent of each set, aromatic rings of a size other than five or six in up to 11.5 percent, and rings of eight or more atoms in 53.4 percent of one set. Diversity is real early (300-615 distinct Murcko scaffolds per 870) and narrows at the top (14-67 scaffolds per 87 top-decile molecules). The Parent pairing is complete: all 15 published n-1744a1494180 trajectories and all 15 staging trajectories were present and read at 300 records each, no path was missing, and the two chemistry profiles are near-indistinguishable on every counter I measured, the largest differences being four-membered rings on one set (30.9 against 13.1 percent) and proposals of four or fewer heavy atoms overall (139 against 97 of 4,350).

per_task.generated_character: 870 proposals, mean 23.6 heavy atoms, MW 362, logP 4.07, TPSA 54, 2.92 rings of which 2.33 aromatic, QED 0.57, SA 3.48 - the most ordinary-looking set of the five. One family owns the upper half: an alkyl/alkoxy-substituted indole-2-carboxamide whose amide goes to pyridin-3-yl or phenyl, descended from the initial trimethoxyindole-2-carboxamide COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC at 0.3051. 335 distinct Murcko scaffolds over the 870, but the top decile holds only 21 and 23 of its 87 molecules share the scaffold of O=C(Nc1cccnc1)c1cc2ccccc2[nH]1. The molecules would be makeable except for one feature: the indole nitrogen is capped with F, Cl or Br in 66 of the 87 top-decile molecules, and 421 of the 870 proposals carry an N-halogen bond. No proposal has a sulfonamide, a sulfone or a saturated six-membered N ring, 27 have a biaryl bond and exactly one has an aryl nitrile.
liabilities: N-fluoro and N-bromo heteroaromatic nitrogens in 421 of 870 proposals, including the best molecule
An alpha-ketoamide in the single best molecule; vicinal dicarbonyl in 5 of the top 87
N-acyloxyamine (C(=O)O-N) linkages in 3 of the top 87, hydrolytically and oxidatively labile
An N,N-dibromo oxazine ring in a 0.438799 molecule, not a drawable stable species
40 proposals of four or fewer heavy atoms and 46 ring-free proposals consumed oracle calls
missing_features: A free N-H or N-alkyl indole nitrogen; 66 of the 87 top-decile molecules carry an N-halogen there instead
An aryl nitrile: 1 of 870 proposals contains one, and none of the top 87 does
Biaryl or fused diazine extension of the core; only 27 of 870 proposals have any aryl-aryl bond and none of the top 87
Polar or basic solubilising groups: zero sulfonamides and sulfones, 65 of 870 with a basic amine and 0 of the top 87
Any polyhalogenated carbon; zero CF3 and at most three fluorine atoms per molecule in this set
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score tracks size, aromatic ring count and the presence of an aryl amide: the top decile averages 25.0 heavy atoms and 2.74 aromatic rings against 10.3 and 0.82 in the bottom decile, whose members are fragments such as FCl and CCl at 0.0. Above 0.43 the gradient goes flat to halogen identity - ten molecules in the top 100 tie at exactly 0.438799 and differ only in F/Br/Cl placement and in OC versus CH3 on the benzo ring - while the best halogen-free proposal reaches only 0.3376 against 0.4403 for the best halogen-bearing one. The reward looks like a fixed lipophilic bicyclic heteroaromatic bearing one anilide-type amide, with no further credit for the peripheral halogen permutations the late budget is spent on.

per_task.generated_character: 870 proposals, mean 32.6 heavy atoms, MW 470, 4.31 rings of which 3.79 aromatic, TPSA 131, QED 0.29 with 55.1 percent below 0.3, SA 4.26 - the least drug-like set. Two leader families. One is a tricyclic pyrazolo-fused thioxo-pyrimidinone bearing a 4-substituted quinazoline on the pyrazole nitrogen and an N-CH(F)-O-CH2Cl chain on the imide nitrogen. The other is a polysubstituted aza-indene carrying two C-nitroso groups, an acetyl and an aldehyde, plus a cyclopropa-fused aniline. 356 Murcko scaffolds overall but only 14 in the top decile. The leaders are not makeable as drawn: 15 of the 87 top-decile molecules carry an O-halogen bond, 42 a C-nitroso, 40 an aldehyde, 43 a four-membered ring and 20 an aromatic ring whose size is neither five nor six.
liabilities: O-F hypofluorite bonds in 89 proposals and 15 of the top 87, including all three 0.8561 molecules
Chloromethyl ether and alpha-fluoro ether alkylating groups in 7 each of the top 50
C-nitroso in 42 and aldehyde in 40 of the top 87, with ring thiones alongside
Peroxide O-O bonds in 83 of 870 proposals, though none in the top 87
Cyclopropa- and cyclobuta-fused benzene rings in the second leader family
missing_features: An ordinary aryl methyl ether or phenol at the position that pays the largest single score step; oxygen arrived there only as an O-F hypofluorite
A sulfone or sulfonamide alternative to the ring thione; zero of 870 proposals contain either
Basic or saturated solubilising chemistry: basic amines in 40 of 870 and in 1 of the top 87, one saturated six-membered N ring in 870
Feasible five- and six-membered closures in place of the strained ones the leaders use; 43 of the top 87 carry a four-membered ring
Written configuration: 50 of the 87 top-decile molecules have at least one unassigned stereocentre
per_task.score_gradient_reading: 0.5 is a floor paid to any valid molecule, including Cl and C=C, so the real range is 0.5 to 0.8561. Score climbs with size and polarity (top decile 36.2 heavy atoms and TPSA 162 against 19.0 and 68 in the bottom decile) and with the quinazoline-on-ring-nitrogen attachment. The decisive step is a single oxygen insertion: the same leader scored 0.6096 carrying cc(F)c(Cl) on the quinazoline (evaluation 269, seed 0) and 0.8561 once that fluorine became an O-F (evaluation 281), so about 0.25 of the 0.36 total range was bought by putting an oxygen on that ring. Only two substituents were ever enumerated at that position in the session, F and OF, and the best halogen-free proposal in the whole set reaches 0.6442.

per_task.generated_character: 870 proposals, mean 30.1 heavy atoms, MW 452, logP 5.30, TPSA 45, 4.02 rings split 2.06 aromatic and 1.96 aliphatic, fsp3 0.38, QED 0.49, SA 4.24 - the most sp3-rich and most lipophilic set, and 405 Murcko scaffolds. The leaders are one recognisable pharmacophore: a basic 1,4-diazepane whose distal nitrogen is linked by -CH2CH2- to a bromo-benzocyclobutene, with a 3-chlorophenyl on the ring carbon that sits between the two nitrogens. All 87 top-decile molecules carry a basic amine and all 87 carry at least one unassigned stereocentre; their mean TPSA is 21 and mean logP 5.50. 241 of the 870 proposals contain an aminal N-C-N centre, 43 of the top 50 do, and not one proposal in 870 contains a saturated piperazine ring.
liabilities: Aminal (N-C-N) centres in 241 of 870 proposals and 67 of the top 87, labile to hydrolysis back to ketone plus diamine
A free thiol in a 1.0-scoring molecule and in 4 of the top 50
Four-membered rings in 65 of the 87 top-decile molecules, including the benzocyclobutene of the best molecules
Strained N-substituted azetine enamines in the seed-2 endgame molecules
O-halogen bonds in 77 proposals and a top-decile mean logP of 5.50
missing_features: A plain aryl-piperazine or aryl-piperidine; zero saturated piperazines and only 3 strict piperidine-type rings in 870 proposals
A hydrolytically stable attachment of the aryl group to the amine ring; 43 of the top 50 put it on a carbon flanked by two nitrogens
Written configuration at the two stereocentres every leader carries (87 of 87 top-decile molecules are stereochemically unspecified)
Any polar group to pull logP back under 5; the top decile has TPSA 21 and no acceptor besides the ring nitrogens
An unstrained fused bicycle in place of the benzocyclobutene; 65 of the top 87 contain a four-membered ring
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The objective is effectively saturated at 1.0 and the gradient is about basicity and lipophilicity rather than size: the top decile averages 27.2 heavy atoms against 29.1 in the bottom decile but carries a basic amine in 87 of 87 against 0 of 87, TPSA 21 against 81 and logP 5.50 against 3.97. The bottom decile is the inherited 3,5-dichlorobenzenesulfonyl proline family at 0.0002, so polar, acidic and sulfonamide molecules sit at the floor; the best amine-free proposal reaches 0.8317 against 1.0 with an amine. What is rewarded is a protonatable ring nitrogen two carbons from a halogenated fused aromatic, and the generator supplies that with a seven-membered aminal-containing ring rather than a piperazine.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score rises steeply with fluorine count and ring count: the best proposal with four or more halogens reaches 0.6823, the best with at most one reaches 0.4246 and the best halogen-free proposal only 0.3088, while the bottom decile is single atoms and diatomics (F at 0.0) averaging 12.0 heavy atoms and 1.40 rings. transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-189cd716f027 on the complete current-profile Search panel: seeds 0, 1 and 2, five objectives, 300 evaluations and 870 optimizer proposals each, 4,350 proposals in total, batch size 10. Not one of the 4,350 proposals contains a trifluoromethyl group and none contains a trifluoromethoxy group. Two halogens on the same carbon occur in at most 1.5 percent of any one objective's 870 proposals (0.0, 1.5, 0.5, 0.0 and 0.5 percent), and the largest fluorine count reached anywhere is six atoms in one molecule, with four of the five sets peaking at three to five. On the set where attainment rises with fluorine count the best proposal carrying four or more halogens scored 0.6823 while the best with at most one scored 0.4246 and the best halogen-free one 0.3088, so the ceiling the generator reaches there is set by how many separate positions it can decorate rather than by how fluorinated a substituent it can make.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot build a polyhalogenated carbon substituent; halogens arrive one atom per heavy atom.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Substituent operators need to be able to add a second and a third halogen to a carbon that already carries one, and to attach prefabricated fluoroalkyl and fluoroalkoxy units in a single edit. At present halogenation is a one-per-site decoration, so any objective whose gradient rewards a locally fluorine-dense group is reachable only by spreading halogens over unrelated positions.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-189cd716f027 on the complete current-profile Search panel: seeds 0, 1 and 2, five objectives, 300 evaluations and 870 optimizer proposals each, 4,350 proposals in total, batch size 10. 818 proposals contain an N-halogen bond and 378 an O-halogen bond; on two sets these dominate the leaders, with 66 of 87 and 53 of 87 top-decile molecules carrying an N-halogen and 15 of 87 on two other sets carrying an O-halogen, including the highest-scoring molecule of one objective. The sharpest case is a single-edit comparison inside one session: the same leader scored 0.6096 with an aryl C-F on a pendant azine (evaluation 269, seed 0) and 0.8561 after an oxygen was inserted into that bond to give an aryl O-F (evaluation 281), about 0.25 of that objective's whole 0.36 dynamic range. The only two substituents ever enumerated at that position in the session were F and OF, so the generator had no ordinary aryl-oxygen route to the feature the gradient was paying for.
transferable_gaps.gap: Halogen is bonded to ring nitrogen and to oxygen as freely as to carbon, and heteroatom halogenation is the generator's only route to some substituents.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Halogen attachment should be restricted to carbon, and hydroxyl, methoxy and related oxygen substituents should be directly available as substitution products, so that reaching an oxygen substituent does not require inserting an atom into a carbon-halogen bond. As it stands the generator converts a chemically impossible group into score, which both wastes the oracle budget on unmakeable leaders and hides the real substituent the gradient wants.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-189cd716f027 on the complete current-profile Search panel: seeds 0, 1 and 2, five objectives, 300 evaluations and 870 optimizer proposals each, 4,350 proposals in total, batch size 10. A fully saturated six-membered ring containing nitrogen occurs in 0, 1, 26, 18 and 0 of each objective's 870 proposals, and a saturated piperazine ring in 0 of 4,350. A saturated seven-membered azacycle reaches 14.0 percent on one set and rings of eight or more atoms reach 53.4 percent on another, where 73 of the 87 top-decile molecules contain one and ring sizes run to 15 atoms. The set that reached its ceiling did so with a seven-membered diazepane whose aryl group sits on the carbon between the two nitrogens: CC1(c2cccc(Cl)c2)NCCCCN1CCc1cc(Br)c2c(c1)CC2F at 1.0, and 43 of its 50 highest-scoring molecules contain that N-C-N aminal. An aryl bonded directly to a saturated ring nitrogen appears in only 1 to 19 percent of proposals.
transferable_gaps.gap: Saturated five- and six-membered nitrogen rings are nearly absent while seven-membered and larger rings are produced freely.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring-forming and ring-expansion operators need a size prior that favours five- and six-membered rings, the ability to close a saturated six-ring between two existing nitrogens, and a direct nitrogen-to-aryl bond-forming edit. Without them the generator expresses a basic ring amine only through larger rings and aminal carbons, so the motif it does find is both less stable and less tunable than the standard one.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-189cd716f027 on the complete current-profile Search panel: seeds 0, 1 and 2, five objectives, 300 evaluations and 870 optimizer proposals each, 4,350 proposals in total, batch size 10. Four-membered rings appear in 9.5, 21.7, 37.1, 30.9 and 24.5 percent of the five sets and aromatic rings of a size other than five or six in up to 11.5 percent. These are not confined to low scorers: 65 of 87 and 43 of 87 top-decile molecules on two sets contain a four-membered ring, 20 and 16 of 87 contain an aromatic ring of unusual size, and the single highest-scoring molecule of one objective, CCCC1c2[nH]n3c2CC(C(=O)N(C)CC3=O)N1Cc1nc(C)cc2ccccc12 at 0.2255, carries a four-membered aromatic diazete fused to an eight-membered ring. Three-membered rings reach 4.7 percent on another set.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring closures are valence-checked but not geometry-checked, so four-membered and non-five/six-membered aromatic rings appear in the leaders.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring operators should carry a feasibility screen on ring size, aromatic ring size and bridge connectivity, with a repair or resample path that offers a feasible alternative instead of rejecting the edit outright. The current behaviour lets the search climb on cores no chemist could make, so an apparent gain is not transferable to a real molecule even when the gradient is read correctly.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-189cd716f027 on the complete current-profile Search panel: seeds 0, 1 and 2, five objectives, 300 evaluations and 870 optimizer proposals each, 4,350 proposals in total, batch size 10. The digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 and charged_rate 0.0 on all five objectives, yet RDKit finds at least one unassigned stereocentre in 30.3, 49.0, 95.1, 75.6 and 68.0 percent of the five sets; in the top deciles that is 87 of 87, 85 of 87 and 78 of 87 on three of them. Leaders such as CC1Cc2cc(CCN3CCCCNC3(C)c3cccc(Cl)c3)cc(Br)c21 at 1.0 and CCCC1c2[nH]n3c2CC(C(=O)N(C)CC3=O)N1Cc1nc(C)cc2ccccc12 at 0.2255 each carry two unspecified centres, so one submitted string stands for four distinct stereoisomers. Basic amine centres, present in 711 of 870 proposals on one set, are always written neutral and no protonated or zwitterionic form is ever proposed.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits constitution only: no written stereochemistry and no charge state, although most of its best molecules are stereogenic.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Operators that create a stereocentre should set or explicitly resolve its configuration, and cases that are achiral or configurationally unstable should be marked as such rather than left blank. The same applies to protonation and tautomer state: the generator currently cannot express either, so it cannot search over them even where the scoring surface plainly depends on the three-dimensional or ionised form.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-189cd716f027 on the complete current-profile Search panel: seeds 0, 1 and 2, five objectives, 300 evaluations and 870 optimizer proposals each, 4,350 proposals in total, batch size 10. 139 of the 4,350 proposals have four or fewer heavy atoms and 156 contain no ring at all. Fragments that reached the oracle include F, Cl, C=C, CCl and FCl, every one of them scoring at its objective's floor - 0.0 on three objectives and the constant 0.5 that one objective pays for any valid molecule. At 300 evaluations per objective that is about 3 percent of the budget, and it is worst on two of the five sets (40 and 39 of 870). The code Parent n-1744a1494180 shows the same path at 97 of 4,350 under the identical panel.
transferable_gaps.gap: Trimming and deletion paths reduce candidates to one- to four-atom fragments, and those fragments are sent to the oracle.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Emitted candidates should pass a minimum heavy-atom and ring-count guard with a resample, so that an operator that strips a molecule to a fragment costs a proposal rather than an oracle call. The guard belongs on emission rather than on the operator, since the same fragments recur late in sessions after the pool has already found far larger leaders.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-189cd716f027 on the complete current-profile Search panel: seeds 0, 1 and 2, five objectives, 300 evaluations and 870 optimizer proposals each, 4,350 proposals in total, batch size 10. Top-decile counts include C-nitroso in 42 and aldehyde in 40 of 87 on one set, chloromethyl ether and alpha-fluoro ether in 7 each of another set's top 50 (both in O=c1c2c3n(-c4ncnc5cc(OF)c(Cl)cc45)nc2n(c(=S)n1C(F)OCCl)C3 at 0.8561), a free thiol in 4 of a third set's top 50 (FC1Cc2cc(CCN3CCCCNC3(CS)c3cccc(Cl)c3)cc(Br)c21 at 1.0), cumulated double bonds in 8 of 87 (N=c1c2cn(C3C(O)=C=C=C3CF)cc2n(CCF)c(=O)n1F) and non-aromatic enols in 26 of 87. Over whole sets, peroxide O-O bonds reach 83 of 870, aminals 241 of 870 and N-O single bonds up to 25 percent of a single set.
transferable_gaps.gap: Reactive and short-lived functional groups are attached as ordinary decorations, including inside the highest-scoring families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A functional-group plausibility screen with conventional replacements is needed on emission, so that a bond-order or heteroatom edit which creates an alkylating, oxidising or self-destroying group is replaced by a stable isostere that keeps the same substitution pattern. The screen has to offer an alternative rather than only reject, because these groups currently sit on otherwise reasonable cores that the search has already paid to find.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-189cd716f027 on the complete current-profile Search panel: seeds 0, 1 and 2, five objectives, 300 evaluations and 870 optimizer proposals each, 4,350 proposals in total, batch size 10. Top-decile scaffold counts collapse to 14 and 21 of 87 molecules on two objectives (against 300 to 615 distinct Murcko scaffolds over each full set of 870), and the repeated scores show the swaps are invisible to the gradient: ten molecules in one top 100 tie at exactly 0.438799 differing only in F, Cl or Br placement and in methoxy versus methyl, and eleven in another tie at 0.622633. On a third objective the top 100 holds 95 distinct scores, so the plateau is a property of what the operators change rather than of the scoring surface.
transferable_gaps.gap: Once a family is established, elaboration is restricted to peripheral swaps the objective scores identically.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs core-level transformations - ring replacement, ring-size change, linker exchange - that survive the identity and duplicate filters once peripheral edits stop changing the score, and a way to recognise that a run of identical scores means its current edit class is exhausted. At present the late budget is spent enumerating terminal heteroatom permutations of a scaffold that is already saturated.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

Accepted-only radius-two chirality-aware 2048-bin integer Morgan-count GP with generalized dot-product Tanimoto kernel, raw mean and population-SD normalization with 0.001 floor, noise SD 0.05, float64 covariance and Cholesky with the original jitter ladder, finite guards and fallback routing.

Correlated Thompson fresh-pool allocation (m-000000000006 residual influence, m-000000000007 cross-candidate correlation) with the exact single normal-array draw, sequential availability masks and first-index ties; prospective prediction and feedback diagnostics.

NEW: stall-conditioned residual amplitude. A session-local consecutive non-improving announced-batch counter (reset on a strictly improving batch) multiplies only the sampled residual by 1.5 while the counter is at least 3, with factor 1.0 otherwise, plus passive same-pool replay diagnostics that use no random numbers.
